paragraphs: John B. Sanfilippo & Son, Inc. was formed as a corporation under the laws of the State of Delaware in 1979 as the successor by merger to an Illinois corporation that was incorporated in 1959. As used throughout this annual report on Form 10-K (this "Report"), unless the context otherwise indicates, the terms "we", "us", "our" or "Company" collectively refer to John B. Sanfilippo & Son, Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiary, JBSS Ventures, LLC. Our fiscal year ends on the final Thursday of June each year, and typically consists of fifty-two weeks (four thirteen-week quarters). Additional information on the comparability of the periods presented is as follows:
• References herein to fiscal 2027 are to the fiscal year ending June 24, 2027.
• References herein to fiscal 2026, fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024 are to the fiscal years ended June 25, 2026, June 26, 2025 and June 27, 2024, respectively.

We are one of the leading processors and distributors of peanuts, pecans, cashews, walnuts, almonds and other nuts in the United States. We also manufacture and distribute a portfolio of snack and nutrition bars ("bars"), and market and distribute, and in most cases, manufacture or process, a diverse product line of other food and snack products, including peanut butter, almond butter, cashew butter, candy and confections, snack and trail mixes, granola, sunflower kernels, dried fruit, corn snacks, sesame sticks and other sesame snack products. We primarily sell our products under a variety of private brand names, as well as under our Fisher, Orchard Valley Harvest, Squirrel Brand and Southern Style Nuts brand names. Our products are sold through three core distribution channels, including food retailers in the consumer channel, commercial ingredient users and contract manufacturing customers.

Our website is accessible to the public at http://www.jbssinc.com. Information about us, including our code of ethics, annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K and any amendments to those reports are made available free of charge through our website as soon as reasonably practicable after such reports have been filed with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC"). Our materials filed with the SEC are also available on the SEC's website at http://www.sec.gov. References to our website addressed in this Form 10-K are provided as a convenience and do not constitute, and should not be viewed as, an incorporation by reference of the information contained on, or available through, the website. Therefore, such information should not be considered part of this Form 10-K.
Our headquarters and executive offices are located at 1703 North Randall Road, Elgin, Illinois 60123, and our telephone number for investor relations is (847) 289-1800, extension 4612.

We operate in a single reporting unit and operating segment that consists of selling various nut and nut related products and bars through three distribution channels with a similar distribution model. See Part II, Item 8 — "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" for our net sales, net income and total assets.

We are one of the leading processors and distributors of tree nuts and peanuts in the United States, and we also manufacture and distribute a complete portfolio of private brand bars. We primarily manufacture and distribute private brand products, as well as manufacture and market nut products under the Fisher, Orchard Valley Harvest, Squirrel Brand and Southern Style Nuts brand names. Through a deliberate strategy of focused capital expenditures and complementary acquisitions, we have built a generally vertically integrated nut processing operation that enables us to control almost every step of the process for pecans, peanuts and walnuts, including procurement from growers, shelling, processing, packaging and marketing. Vertical integration allows us to enhance product quality and, in most crop years, purchase inshell pecans, peanuts and walnuts from growers at lower costs as opposed to purchasing these nut meats from other shellers. We believe that our business model typically works to our advantage in terms of increased cost savings for raw materials and provides us with better insight into crop development.

Our manufacturing experience, operations knowledge and product reputation in the tree nut and peanut private brand business has allowed us to launch and expand our private brand bars business over the past five years. We believe there are significant growth opportunities in the private brand bar business as well as opportunities for us to bring our experience in the snack category and innovation to expand our private brand bar business. We have made capital investments to support and expand the bar business in the last two fiscal years.

Our brands are some of the most well-recognized in the packaged food industry. In recent years, we have developed Fisher recipe nuts among the leading brands in the category through strong marketing campaigns, merchandising, and promotional support to retailers. We launched innovation with our Orchard Valley Harvest and increased distribution on our Fisher snack nut brands and also expanded into alternative channels with Southern Style Nuts and Squirrel Brand. Our branded and private brand products are sold through the major distribution channels to significant buyers of nuts, including food and other retailers (both brick and mortar and e-commerce), commercial ingredient users and contract manufacturing customers. Selling through multiple distribution channels allows us to generate multiple revenue opportunities for the products we process. For example, pecan halves could be sold to food retailers under our Fisher brand, and pecan pieces could be sold to commercial ingredient users. We process and sell all major nut types consumed in the United States, including peanuts, pecans, cashews, walnuts and almonds (our major nut types). These are sold in a wide variety of innovative packaging, which provides our customers a complete nut product offering.

Our principal products are raw and processed nuts and bars. Including trail and snack mixes, these nut and bar products accounted for approximately 93% of our gross sales for fiscal 2026, and 92% for fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024. The nut product line includes almonds, pecans, peanuts, walnuts, cashews, macadamia nuts, pistachios, pine nuts and filberts. Our nut products are sold in numerous package styles and sizes, and we offer our nut products in a variety of different styles and seasonings. The bar product line includes chewy granola, fruit and grain, sweet and salty, dipped chewy granola, crunchy, energy, fiber, nut, fig and protein bars. We sell our products domestically to retailers and wholesalers as well as to commercial ingredient and contract manufacturing customers. For more information about our revenues in our various distribution channels, see Part II, Item 8 — "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data".

Furthermore, we manufacture and market peanut butter in several sizes and varieties. We also market and distribute, and in many cases process and manufacture, a wide assortment of other food and snack products. These other products include salad toppings, dried fruit and chocolate and yogurt coated products sold to retailers and wholesalers. Recipe ingredients are sold to retailers, wholesalers and commercial ingredient customers. Additionally, bulk food products are sold to commercial ingredient users. Moreover, an assortment of sunflower kernels, pepitas, snack mixes, almond butter, cashew butter, candy and confections, corn snacks, sesame sticks and other sesame snack products are sold to retail supermarkets, mass merchandisers and commercial ingredient users with a wide variety of toppings for ice cream and yogurt sold to commercial ingredient users.

We sell our products to approximately 200 customers through the consumer, commercial ingredient and contract manufacturing distribution channels. The consumer channel is our largest channel by sales and supplies nut-based and bar products, including consumer-packaged products, to retailers in the United States including supermarket chains, wholesalers, supercenters, internet retailers and other retail outlets. We sell products through the consumer channel under our brand names, including the Fisher, Orchard Valley Harvest, Squirrel Brand, and Southern Style Nuts brands, as well as under our customers' private brands. The commercial ingredient channel supplies nut-based products to other manufacturers to use as ingredients in their final food products such as bakery, confection and cereal. This channel produces nut-based products that are customized to the specifications of chefs, national restaurant chains, foodservice distributors, fast food chains and hotel kitchens. We sell products through the commercial ingredient channel under our Fisher brand and our customers' private brands. Our contract manufacturing channel primarily processes and packages nut and fruit-based snacks for other food companies under their brand names and in accordance with their specifications.

We are dependent on a few significant customers for a majority of our total net sales, particularly in the consumer channel. Net sales to Walmart Inc. accounted for approximately 41% of our net sales for fiscal 2026, 40% of our net sales for fiscal 2025 and 39% of our net sales for fiscal 2024. Net sales to Target Corporation accounted for approximately 12% of our net sales for fiscal 2026, 11% for fiscal 2025 and 13% for fiscal 2024. No other customer accounted for more than 10% of net sales for any period presented.

paragraphs: We face a number of significant risks and uncertainties, and therefore, an investment in our Common Stock is subject to risks and uncertainties. The factors described below could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition. While each risk is described separately, some of these risks are interrelated and it is possible that certain risks could trigger the applicability of other risks described below. Also, the risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones that we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or risks we view as not rising to the level of being material, could also potentially impair our business, results of operations and financial condition. Investors should consider the following factors, in addition to the other information contained in this Report, including Part II, Item 7 — "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations — Liquidity and Capital Resources" before deciding to purchase our Common Stock.

The availability and cost of raw materials for producing our products are subject to crop size and yield fluctuations caused by factors beyond our control. These materials include peanuts, pecans, almonds, cashews, walnuts, pine nuts and other nuts, rolled oats, dried fruits and seeds, cocoa, protein, as well as vegetable oils and other products used in the manufacture of our products. The factors beyond our control include adverse weather conditions, natural disasters (including floods, torrential rain, hail, mudslides, tornados, droughts, frosts, earthquakes and hurricanes), changing climate patterns, agricultural diseases and pests, foreign currency fluctuations, trade agreements, tariffs and embargos, import/export controls, prices of other crops, labor shortages, inflationary conditions, political change and unrest, sanctions, boycotts, revised sourcing regulations, armed hostilities, such as those in Ukraine and in the Middle East, changes in fuel prices, changes in global customer demand, pandemics and disease, changes in government agricultural programs, government support of any agricultural products, federal and state government mandates related to the preceding or otherwise and purchasing behavior of certain countries, including China and India. Additionally, any determination by the USDA or other government agencies may also reduce the supply of edible nuts and other raw materials used in our products and could (among other things) cause our costs to increase significantly. These determinations include, but are not limited to, that certain pesticides, herbicides or other chemicals used by growers have left harmful residues on portions of the crop, negatively impact the environment, cause or may cause adverse health consequences, any portion of the crop has been contaminated by aflatoxin or other agents, or any future raw material or product recalls for other reasons.

Because these raw materials are commodities, their prices are set by the market and can therefore fluctuate quickly and dramatically due to varied events, such as those described above. Furthermore, we are not able to hedge against changes in nut commodity prices because no appropriate futures, derivative or other risk-sharing market for these commodities exists nor can we create such a market. Consequently, in order to achieve or maintain profitability levels, we attempt to increase the prices of our products to reflect the increase in the costs of the raw materials that we use. However, we may not be successful in passing along partial or full price increases to our customers, if at all. In addition, even if we are successful in passing across partial or full price increases, we may not be able to do so in a timely fashion. Our ability to raise prices and the timing of any price increases is often dependent upon the actions of our competitors, some of whom are significantly larger and more diversified than we are or own farms which produce the raw materials subject to such price increases. Determining the alignment of commodity costs with customer pricing also requires significant coordination throughout our entire operations and we may not be able to successfully manage such coordination in the future to align commodity costs with customer prices. We have observed rapid inflation with respect to packaging and other products used to manufacture and package our products and general inflationary conditions that are difficult to predict, and we may not be able to pass along such inflationary increases to our customers or may not be able to do so in a timely fashion. We have also observed tariffs and the threat of tariffs causing increased or uncertain changes in prices and uncertainty in the markets in which we operate, including for the purchase of certain equipment for the manufacture of products. Additionally, any such product price increase that we are able to pass along to our customers may ultimately reduce the demand for, and sales of, our products as customers reduce purchases, buy lower priced products or lower margin products. Alternatively, if the prices of any raw materials significantly decrease, and we have inventories of such materials on hand, we may be unable to reduce product prices without adversely impacting our gross margins or our customers will not pass along price decreases, which could impact overall demand for such products. Any competitors who purchase such material on the open market or own the farms which produce the raw materials may be able to reduce prices in a more timely manner, and we could lose market share to such competitors. We are also subject to risks associated with purchasing a majority of our pecans, peanuts and walnuts directly from growers, including the risk of purchasing such products from growers at costs that later, due to altered market conditions, prove to be above prevailing market prices at time of sale. Accordingly, because we purchase a majority of our pecans, peanuts and walnuts directly from growers during harvest season and shell and process these nuts throughout our fiscal year, there is a possibility that, after we acquire these nuts, market conditions may adversely change. Depending on these changing market conditions, we may be forced to sell these nuts at reduced prices relative to our acquisition cost. Any one or more of the foregoing aspects may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

Moreover, fluctuations in the market prices of nuts may affect the value of our inventories, margins and profitability. We enter into fixed price commitments with a portion of our commercial ingredient customers. The commitments are for a fixed period of time, typically three months to twelve months. Such commitments with a term of six months or more represented approximately 1% of our annual net sales in fiscal 2026. Sometimes we enter into fixed price commitments with respect to certain nut products before fixing our acquisition costs in order to maintain customer relationships or when, in management's judgment, market or crop harvest conditions so warrant. To the extent we do so and our fixed prices are not properly aligned with our acquisition costs, these fixed price commitments may result in reduced or negative gross profit margins, which could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.

We operate in a highly competitive environment. The principal areas of competition are, among others, taste, flavor, quality, packaging, price, nutrition, brand recognition, advertising, promotion, convenience and service. Our principal products compete against food and snack products manufactured and sold by numerous regional, national and international companies, some of which are substantially larger and have greater resources than us, such as Hormel Foods Corp. (Planters brand), Diamond Brand, General Mills (Nature Valley brand), PepsiCo, Inc. (Quaker brand), Mondelez (CLIF brand), Kellanova (Nutrigrain brand), Mars (KIND brand), and others. Most of our competitors that sell and market the other top branded snack nut products and bars have committed more financial, marketing and other resources to such brands when compared to the resources available to or spent by us on our brands. Additionally, many food retailers, supercenters, mass merchandisers and internet retailers have continued to emphasize their own private brand offerings as a key part of their strategy and may develop or expand their own private brand nut and nut product offerings and private brand bar offerings, to the exclusion of our branded products or private brand products, particularly in an uncertain economic environment or due to inflationary conditions. Certain other grocery retailers, such as international stores or smaller format stores, may not stock our products. Other smaller competitors may be able to focus on faster-growing, niche markets that we are unable to market effectively to or otherwise sell to due to our size, operations, marketing strategy or perceptions regarding our Company. Additionally, certain food retailers and internet retailers may seek to invest in companies serving certain niche markets and/or offer shelf space, added promotional activity or other marketing efforts in exchange for ownership in such companies, which we are unable to offer to such food retailers or internet companies. Recent consolidation and mergers and acquisitions activity in the nut and snack food industry has intensified competitive pricing pressures across the market. Many of our competitors buy their nuts on the open market and are thus not exposed to the risks of purchasing inshell pecans, peanuts, walnuts and other nut types directly from growers at fixed prices that later, due to altered market conditions, may prove to be above prevailing market prices. We also compete with other shellers in the commercial ingredients market and with regional processors in the retail and wholesale markets. In order to maintain or increase our market share, we must continue to price our products competitively and spend on marketing, advertising, new product innovation and shelf placement and slotting fees. This may cause a decline in gross profit margin if we are unable to increase sales volume or otherwise reduce our costs, which could materially and adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.

Some customer buying decisions, including some of our largest private brand customers, are based upon a periodic bidding process in which a single, successful bidder is assured the right to sell the selected product or products to the food retailer, supercenter, mass merchandiser, club store or internet retailer until the next bidding process to the exclusion of other bidders. Our sales volume may decrease significantly if our bids are too high and we lose the ability to sell products through these channels, even temporarily. Alternatively, we risk reducing our margins if our bids are successful, but below our desired price points. In addition, our margins could be further reduced if commodity prices or other input prices subsequently rise and customers are unwilling or unable to accept price increases. The nut and snack food industry has experienced consolidation and significant mergers and acquisitions activity in recent years. If certain of our competitors elect to reduce prices in order to increase sales or market share, our market share could decrease and this could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.

The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements. Our fiscal year ends on the final Thursday of June each year and typically consists of fifty-two weeks (four thirteen-week quarters). Additional information on the comparability of the periods presented is as follows:
• References herein to fiscal 2027 are to the fiscal year ending June 24, 2027.
• References herein to fiscal 2026, fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024 are to the fiscal years ended June 25, 2026, June 26, 2025 and June 27, 2024, respectively.

As used herein, unless the context otherwise indicates, the terms "we", "us", "our" or "Company" collectively refer to John B. Sanfilippo & Son, Inc. and our wholly-owned subsidiary, JBSS Ventures, LLC.

We are one of the leading processors and distributors of peanuts, pecans, cashews, walnuts, almonds and other nuts in the United States. We also manufacture and distribute a portfolio of snack and nutrition bars ("bars"), and market and distribute, and in most cases, manufacture or process, a diverse product line of other food and snack products, including peanut butter, almond butter, cashew butter, candy and confections, snack and trail mixes, granola, sunflower kernels, dried fruit, corn snacks, sesame sticks and other sesame snack products. We primarily sell our products under a variety of private brand names, as well as under our Fisher, Orchard Valley Harvest, Squirrel Brand and Southern Style Nuts brand names. Our products are sold through three core distribution channels, including food retailers in the consumer channel, commercial ingredient users and contract manufacturing customers.

Our Long-Range Plan defines our future growth priorities, including accelerating our private brand business with key customers in high-growth snacking categories, most notably private brand bars. The Long-Range Plan also emphasizes expanding branded distribution behind Orchard Valley Harvest and Fisher via insight-driven product and packaging innovation in our consumer and commercial ingredients channels, while strategically partnering with leading brands in our contract manufacturing channel. Execution of the Long-Range Plan is anchored in delivering value-added solutions and high-quality, innovative products based on our extensive industry and consumer expertise. Growth in private brand bars will be supported by our ongoing capacity expansion and a robust innovation pipeline, with continued focus on nutrition and protein bars. For our branded nut and trail mix business, we are focused on attracting new consumers through product innovation, broader distribution across traditional and alternative channels and expanded purchasing occasions, including club stores and e-commerce. Promotional and advertising investments are being prioritized to drive branded volume growth, supported by an omni-channel strategy across recipe nuts, snack nuts and trail mix. Our Long-Range Plan includes growth through product and packaging innovation and targeted, opportunistic acquisitions. To support these initiatives, we have made significant capital investments in equipment and infrastructure improvements to expand our production capabilities, improve efficiency and enhance product offerings for our customers.

We continue to face ongoing operational and regulatory challenges, including food safety and compliance requirements, maintaining and expanding our customer base and driving growth across private brand and branded categories. Shifts or declines in consumer demand within a highly competitive snack product environment, combined with macroeconomic uncertainty, could adversely impact our ability to execute our Long-Range Plan.

Additional challenges include higher food and input costs driven by increasing underlying commodity acquisition costs as well as actual, potential or threatened U.S. and foreign tariffs on key commodities, raw materials and manufacturing equipment. Ongoing uncertainty around global conflict in the Middle East and interest rates may further impact economic growth and consumer spending resulting in reduced demand for private brand and branded snack products, including snack nuts, trail mix and bars. We also continue to operate amid intense industry competition, potential economic downturns in the markets in which we operate and ongoing supply chain volatility. To stay compliant with recent changes in employment laws across states where we operate and remain competitive in attracting qualified talent, we expect our labor costs to continue to increase.

We continue to face changing marketplace trends that impact our categories. Retail prices across snack nuts and trail mix have generally risen due to increased commodity costs and evolving global trade agreements. These higher prices, paired with general economic uncertainty, are causing consumers to purchase fewer snack products. As a result, sales volumes for snack nuts, trail mix and mainstream bars are declining for the Company and the industry overall. Many consumers are shifting to private brands, more affordable nuts or bars or choosing snacks outside these categories altogether. Consumers are also shifting to more value-focused retailers, such as mass merchandising retailers and club stores, not all of which we distribute or sell to. Additionally, emerging health and wellness trends, use of GLP-1 drugs and other consumer health priorities may also impact consumers' purchasing behavior, including decreased purchasing of snack foods. In response, we are focusing on our existing products in our portfolio that address these trends, as well as our strengths by leveraging our expertise in snack nut and trail mix and bars categories, development of
additional products that are on-trend, improving efficiency, innovating in product and packaging and carefully managing trade spending and pricing to support our products.

Global supply chain pressures have eased compared to past fiscal years. However, intermittent challenges, delays and extended lead-times still exist for certain raw materials and inputs. Overall packaging and ingredient inflation appears to have moderated during fiscal 2026. However there is still uncertainty within the supply chain from the U.S. government's tariffs policy on imports from foreign countries and corresponding retaliatory tariffs from foreign countries. Any incremental import tariffs will increase the cost of certain raw materials we use in our business, and our financial performance may be adversely impacted if we cannot pass on the cost increases in the form of price increases to our customers. In November 2025, the U.S. government removed tariffs for several food categories, including cocoa and cashews among others, which have no domestic production.

In February 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that tariffs imposed by executive order under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA") exceeded U.S. Presidential authority. Subsequently, the Court of International Trade ordered U.S. Customs and Border Patrol to develop a framework for refunding such tariffs. Following the Supreme Court ruling, the President implemented a temporary worldwide baseline tariff of 10% under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 (the "Trade Act"). These tariffs are time limited and expired in early fiscal 2027. In March 2026, the U.S. Trade Representative launched several investigations under Section 301 of the Trade Act into the failure of numerous trading partners to prohibit or effectively enforce bans on imports produced with forced labor. These investigations resulted in country-specific additional tariffs imposed by the U.S. President of 10% or 12.5% which became effective on July 24, 2026. These Section 301 tariffs have been challenged as exceeding U.S. Presidential authority. The ongoing and ultimate impact of tariffs may be difficult to predict as their amount and duration are uncertain, making our planning process more difficult. The threat of tariffs may also have adverse implications to our business and the business of our suppliers and customers. We typically are not the importers of record for commodities that we procure from non-U.S. sources. It is uncertain when or if, and in what amount, any eventual tariff refunds our vendors receive may be passed onto us. We are the importers of record for the capital equipment we are purchasing from European vendors and paid approximately $4.0 million in IEEPA tariffs in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, we received a refund of IEEPA tariffs paid of approximately $4.0 million.

While we do not have direct exposure to suppliers in Russia, Ukraine, Iran or Israel, the conflicts and prospects for conflict in these regions could continue to result in volatile commodity markets, supply chain disruptions and increased costs, including energy and shipping costs.

Trucking capacity continues to slowly decline, potentially leading to further instability in the transportation industry. While indicators suggest transportation prices are stabilizing, the overall transportation environment remains unpredictable. Additionally, fuel prices have been unpredictable and may vary depending on economic activity in the areas where we ship and receive goods as well as prevailing oil prices. We have seen fuel prices increase due to recent military operations in and around Iran, which have led to volatility in the price of crude oil. Fuel prices could continue to remain volatile as the conflict persists.

paragraphs: John B. Sanfilippo & Son, Inc. 於 1979 年根據德拉華州法律成立為一家公司，為一間伊利諾州公司透過合併而成為的後繼公司，該伊利諾州公司於 1959 年成立。在本年度報告書（此「報告」）中，除非文意另有明確表示，否則「我們」、「我們」、「我們」或「公司」 collectively 指 John B. Sanfilippo & Son, Inc. 及其全資子公司 JBSS Ventures, LLC。我們的會計年度於每年六月的最後一個星期四結束，通常包含 52 週（四個 13 週季度）。關於所列期間可比性的額外資訊如下：
• 本報告中提及的財務 2027 年，係指 2027 年 6 月 24 日結束的會計年度。
• 本報告中提及的財務 2026 年、財務 2025 年及財務 2024 年，分別係指 2026 年 6 月 25 日結束、2025 年 6 月 26 日結束及 2024 年 6 月 27 日結束的會計年度。

我們是美國花生、堅果、腰果、核桃、杏仁及其他堅果的主要加工與分銷商。我們也製造與分銷一系列零食與營養棒（"棒"），並行銷與分銷，且在大多數情況下製造或處理，多樣化的其他食品與零食產品，包括花生醬、杏仁醬、腰果醬、糖果與甜點、零食與混合堅果、格蘭諾拉穀物、向日葵仁、乾果、玉米零食、芝麻棒及其他芝麻零食產品。我們主要以多種自有品牌名稱銷售產品，以及 Fisher、Orchard Valley Harvest、Squirrel Brand 和 Southern Style Nuts 品牌名稱。我們的產品透過三個核心分銷渠道銷售，包括消費端的食品零售商、商業原料使用者及委製製造客戶。

我們的網站為公眾所使用，網址為 http://www.jbssinc.com。關於我們的資訊，包括我們的倫理準則、年度 10-K 報告、季報 10-Q、現況報告 8-K 以及這些報告的任何修正案，均會在這些報告提交美國證券交易委員會（"SEC"）後儘速於我們的網站上免費提供。我們提交至 SEC 的資料亦可在 SEC 網站 http://www.sec.gov 查閱。本 10-K 報告中提及的網站資訊僅為方便起見，並不構成，也不應視為網站內容或透過網站取得資訊的引用。因此，這些資訊不應視為本 10-K 報告的一部分。
我們的總部及高階管理辦公室位於伊利諾州艾林 1703 北 Randall 路，郵遞區號 60123，我們投資人關係專線電話為 (847) 289-1800，分機 4612。
我們運作於一個單一的報告單位及營運部門，該營運部門包含透過三個分銷渠道銷售各種堅果及相關產品與棒，並採用類似的分銷模式。請參閱第二部分，第 8 項 — "財務報表與補充資料"，以取得我們的淨銷售額、淨收入及總資產資料。

我們是美國樹果及花生的主要加工與分銷商，我們也製造與分銷完整的自有品牌棒產品組合。我們主要製造與分銷自有品牌產品，並製造與行銷樹果產品於 Fisher、Orchard Valley Harvest、Squirrel Brand 和 Southern Style Nuts 品牌名稱下。透過有意圖的資本支出及補充收購策略，我們已建立一個通常垂直整合的堅果加工作業，使我們能控制pecans、花生及核桃的幾乎所有加工步驟，包括從種植者處採購、剝殼、加工、包裝及行銷。垂直整合使我們能提升產品品質，並在大多數收成年份，以較低成本從種植者處購入整殼pecans、花生及核桃，而非從其他剝殼商處購入這些堅果仁。我們認為，我們的商業模式通常對我們有優勢，能帶來原材料成本的增加節省，並使我們對作物發展有更深入的瞭解。
本公司在樹果與花生私有品牌業務的製造經驗、營運知識與產品聲譽，使我們在過去五年內得以發起並擴展私有品牌棒狀零食業務。我們認為私有品牌棒狀零食業務有顯著的成長機會，同時也認為我們在零食類別的經驗與創新，可協助我們擴展私有品牌棒狀零食業務。我們在過去兩個會計年度內已進行資本投資，以支持並擴展棒狀零食業務。

我們的品牌是包裝食品產業中最具知名度的品牌之一。近年來，我們透過強大的行銷活動、商品陳列與促銷支援，將 Fisher 系列堅果發展為該類別中的領導品牌。我們推出了創新產品，包括 Orchard Valley Harvest，並擴大了 Fisher 零食堅果品牌的通路，同時也透過 Southern Style Nuts 和 Squirrel Brand 進入了替代通路。我們的自有品牌與私有品牌產品透過主要通路銷售給重要的堅果買家，包括食品及其他零售商（實體與電商）、商業原料使用者與委製客戶。透過多種通路銷售，使我們能為所處理的產品創造多種收入機會。例如，開心果半顆可透過 Fisher 品牌銷售給食品零售商，而開心果碎則可銷售給商業原料使用者。我們處理並銷售美國消費的所有主要堅果類型，包括花生、開心果、腰果、核桃與杏仁（我們的主要堅果類型）。這些產品以廣泛的創新包裝方式銷售，為客戶提供完整的堅果產品組合。

我們的主要產品為生鮮與加工堅果與棒狀零食。包括小徑與零食混合產品，這些堅果與棒狀零食產品在會計年度 2026 的毛利率銷售中佔約 93%，在會計年度 2025 和 2024 則佔 92%。堅果產品線包括杏仁、開心果、花生、核桃、腰果、澳洲堅果、 Pistachios、松子與山核桃。我們的堅果產品以多種包裝風格與尺寸銷售，並提供多種不同風格與調味的堅果產品。棒狀零食產品線包括嚼勁堅果穀物、水果與穀物、甜鹹混合、沾醬嚼勁堅果穀物、酥脆、能量、纖維、堅果、無花果與蛋白質棒狀零食。我們將產品銷售至美國的零售商與經銷商，以及商業原料與委製客戶。如需瞭解我們在不同通路的收入資訊，請參閱第二部分，第 8 項 — "財務資料與補充資料"。

此外，我們製造並行銷多種尺寸與種類的花生醬。我們也行銷並分銷，並在許多情況下處理與製造，廣泛的其他食品與零食產品。這些其他產品包括沙拉配料、乾果與巧克力與優格包覆產品，銷售給零售商與經銷商。食譜原料銷售給零售商、經銷商與商業原料客戶。此外，大宗食品產品銷售給商業原料使用者。此外，種子類產品包括向日葵籽、 pepitas、零食混合、杏仁醬、腰果醬、糖果與甜點、玉米零食、芝麻棒與其他芝麻零食產品，銷售給零售超級市場、大規模零售通路與商業原料使用者，並以廣泛的配料銷售給商業原料使用者的冰淇淋與優格。

我們透過消費者、商業原料與委製製造通路，將產品銷售給約 200 家客戶。消費者通路為我們最大的銷售通路，並供應以堅果與棒狀零食為基礎的產品，包括消費者包裝產品，給美國的零售商，包括超級市場連鎖店、經銷商、超級中心、網路零售商及其他零售通路。我們透過消費者通路以我們的品牌名稱銷售產品，包括 Fisher、Orchard Valley Harvest、Squirrel Brand 和 Southern Style Nuts 品牌，以及我們客戶的私有品牌。商業原料通路供應以堅果為基礎的產品給其他製造商，供其用於最終食品產品中，例如烘焙、甜點與穀物產品。此通路生產以堅果為基礎的產品，並根據廚師、全國連鎖餐廳、食品服務經銷商、速食連鎖店與酒店廚房的規格進行客製化。我們透過商業原料通路以 Fisher 品牌與我們客戶的私有品牌銷售產品。我們的委製製造通路主要為其他食品公司處理與包裝以堅果與水果為基礎的零食，並依照其品牌名稱與規格進行。

我們依賴少數重要的客戶，以產生我們總淨銷售額的大多數，尤其是在消費者通路。銷售給 Walmart Inc. 的淨銷售額在會計年度 2026 佔約 41%，在會計年度 2025 佔約 40%，在會計年度 2024 佔約 39%。銷售給 Target Corporation 的淨銷售額在會計年度 2026 佔約 12%，在會計年度 2025 佔約 11%，在會計年度 2024 佔約 13%。沒有其他客戶在任一報告期間的淨銷售額超過 10%。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析應與合併財務報表及合併財務報表附註一併閱讀。我們的會計年度於每年六月的最後一個星期四結束，通常包含五十二週（四個十三週財季）。關於所列會計期間可比性之額外資訊如下：
• 本文中提及的財務年度 2027 年，係指於 2027 年 6 月 24 日結束之財務年度。
• 本文中提及的財務年度 2026 年、財務年度 2025 年及財務年度 2024 年，係指於 2026 年 6 月 25 日、2025 年 6 月 26 日及 2024 年 6 月 27 日結束之財務年度，分別。
本文中所用之術語 "we"、"us"、"our" 或 "Company"，除非上下文另有說明，否則 collectively 指 John B. Sanfilippo & Son, Inc. 及我們之 wholly-owned subsidiary，JBSS Ventures, LLC。

我們是美國花生、堅果、腰果、核桃、杏仁及其他堅果的主要加工與分銷商。我們也製造與分銷一系列零食與營養棒（"bars"），並行銷與分銷，且在大多數情況下製造或處理，其他種類的食品與零食產品，包括花生醬、杏仁醬、腰果醬、糖果與甜點、零食與混合堅果、格蘭諾拉穀物、向日葵仁、乾果、玉米零食、芝麻棒及其他芝麻零食產品。我們主要以多種私人品牌名稱銷售產品，以及以 Fisher、Orchard Valley Harvest、Squirrel Brand 和 Southern Style Nuts 品牌名稱銷售產品。我們的產品透過三個核心分銷渠道銷售，包括消費端的食品零售商、商業原料使用者及委製客戶。

我們的長期發展計畫定義了我們未來的成長優先事項，包括加速在高成長零食類別中與關鍵客戶合作的私人品牌業務，特別是私人品牌棒狀零食。長期發展計畫也強調透過基於我們在消費端與商業原料渠道的洞察力驅動的產品與包裝創新，擴展 Orchard Valley Harvest 和 Fisher 的品牌分銷。同時，我們在委製製造渠道中與領先品牌進行戰略合作。長期發展計畫的執行以提供附加價值解決方案及基於我們廣泛產業與消費經驗的高品質創新產品為核心。私人品牌棒狀零食的成長將由我們持續的生產能力擴張及強大的創新管道支撐，持續著重於營養與蛋白質棒。針對我們的品牌堅果與混合堅果業務，我們專注於透過產品創新吸引新消費者、在傳統與替代渠道中擴大分銷，以及擴展購買時機，包括俱樂部商店與電商。促銷與廣告投資已優先考量以推動品牌銷售成長，並透過跨通路策略支撐配方堅果、零食堅果與混合堅果的成長。我們的長期發展計畫包含透過產品與包裝創新及針對性、機會性的收購來實現成長。為支持這些計畫，我們已對設備與基礎設施改善進行重大資本投資，以擴展生產能力、提高效率並提升對客戶的產品提供。
我們持續面臨運營與法規上的挑戰，包括食品安全與合規要求、維持與擴展客戶羣以及在私人品牌與品牌類別中推動成長。在高度競爭的零食產品環境中，消費者需求的變化或下降，加上總體經濟的不確定性，可能不利於我們執行長期發展計畫的能力。

額外的挑戰包括因基礎商品採購成本上升所導致的食品與原料成本增加，以及美國與外國對關鍵商品、原材料與製造設備的實際、潛在或威脅性關稅。全球中東地區衝突與利率的持續不確定性可能進一步影響經濟成長與消費者支出，導致私人品牌與品牌零食產品的需求減少，包括零食堅果、混合堅果與棒狀零食。我們也持續在激烈產業競爭、我們營運市場的潛在經濟衰退及供應鏈波動中運作。為符合我們營運州份最近的就業法規變動並在吸引合格人才方面保持競爭力，我們預期勞動成本將持續增加。

本公司持續面臨變動的市場趨勢，影響我們的產品類別。零食堅果與混合堅果條的零售價格因商品原物料成本上升及全球貿易協議的變化，已普遍上漲。這些較高的價格，搭配總體經濟的不確定性，導致消費者購買較少的零食產品。因此，本公司及整個產業的堅果零食、混合堅果條與主流棒狀零食的銷售量正在下降。許多消費者轉向自有品牌、較經濟實惠的堅果或棒狀零食，或完全選擇其他類別的零食。消費者同時也轉向更注重價值的零售通路，例如量販店與俱樂部商店，但並非所有這些通路我們都進貨或銷售。此外，興起的健康與 wellness 趨勢、GLP-1 藥物的使用及其他消費者健康優先事項，也可能影響消費者的購買新鮮食品行為，包括減少零食食品的購買。為此，我們正著重於現有產品組閤中符合這些趨勢的產品，以及我們的優勢，透過我們在堅果零食、混合堅果條與棒狀零食類別的專業知識，開發符合趨勢的產品，提升效率，創新產品與包裝，並謹慎管理貿易支出與價格以支撐我們的產品。

全球供應鏈壓力相比過去財務年度已有所緩和。然而，某些原物料與投入物資仍存在間歇性挑戰、延遲與延長的交貨時間。整體包裝與原料的通貨膨脹似乎在財務年度 2026 年已趨緩。然而，供應鏈中仍存在來自美國政府對進口自外國商品的關稅政策及對應的報復性關稅的不確定性。任何額外的進口關稅將提高我們業務中使用某些原物料的成本，若我們無法將成本增加轉嫁為價格上漲，則可能對我們的財務表現造成不利影響。2025 年 11 月，美國政府已取消若干食品類別的關稅，包括可可與腰果等，這些產品在美國無國內生產。

2026 年 2 月，美國最高法院裁定，根據國際緊急經濟權力法案（"IEEPA"）所課徵的關稅超出了美國總統的權限。隨後，國際貿易法院下令美國邊境巡邏隊制定一個退款框架。在最高法院裁定後，總統根據 1974 年貿易法案第 122 條（"貿易法案"）實施了一項暫時性的全球基礎關稅為 10%。這些關稅有時間限制，並在財務年度 2027 年初到期。2026 年 3 月，美國貿易代表根據貿易法案第 301 條，啟動了對多個貿易夥伴未能禁止或有效執行禁止使用強制勞動生產的進口商品的調查。這些調查導致美國總統課徵了 10% 或 12.5% 的國家特定額外關稅，並於 2026 年 7 月 24 日生效。這些第 301 條關稅被質疑超出美國總統的權限。持續進行及最終的關稅影響可能難以預測，因其金額與持續時間不確定，使我們的規劃過程更加困難。關稅的威脅也可能對我們的業務及我們供應商與客戶的業務產生不利影響。我們通常並非來自非美國來源採購商品的進口記錄人。無法預測任何最終關稅退款我們供應商所收到的金額，以及這些退款是否會轉嫁給我們。我們為購買來自歐洲供應商的資本設備的進口記錄人，並在財務年度 2026 年第三季支付了約 4.0 億美元的 IEEPA 關稅。在財務年度 2026 年第四季，我們收到了約 4.0 億美元的 IEEPA 關稅退款。

2026 年 2 月，美國最高法院裁定，總統依據國際緊急經濟權力法（"IEEPA"）所頒布的關稅，已超出美國總統的權限。隨後，國際貿易法院下令美國海關及邊境保護局開發一個框架，用以退還這些關稅。在最高法院裁決後，總統依據 1974 年貿易法（"貿易法"）第 122 節，實施了一項暫時性的全球基礎關稅為 10%。這些關稅有時間限制，並於 2027 年財務年度初期過期。2026 年 3 月，美國貿易代表辦公室依據貿易法第 301 節，啟動了針對多個貿易夥伴未能禁止或有效執行禁止使用強迫勞動生產的進口商品的調查。這些調查導致美國總統針對某些國家課徵額外關稅，為 10% 或 12.5%，並於 2026 年 7 月 24 日生效。這些第 301 節關稅已被質疑是否超出美國總統的權限。關稅的持續影響與最終結果可能難以預測，因其金額與持續時間不確定，使我們的規劃過程更加困難。關稅的威脅也可能對我們的業務以及我們供應商與客戶的業務產生不利影響。我們通常並非從非美國來源採購商品的進口記錄人。任何最終關稅退款，我們的供應商所收到的金額，可能在何時或是否會轉嫁給我們，仍不確定。我們是從歐洲供應商購買新設備的進口記錄人，並在 2026 年財務年度第三季支付約 4.0 百萬美元的 IEEPA 關稅。在 2026 年財務年度第四季，我們收到約 4.0 百萬美元的 IEEPA 關稅退款。
貨車運輸能力持續緩慢下降，可能導致運輸產業進一步不穩定。雖然指標顯示運輸價格已趨於穩定，但整體運輸環境仍不確定。此外，燃料價格也難以預測，可能因我們運送與接收貨物的地區經濟活動及原油價格而有所變動。我們觀察到因近期伊朗及其周邊地區的軍事行動，導致燃料價格上漲，造成原油價格波動。燃料價格可能持續波動，直到衝突持續。

Trucking capacity continues to slowly decline, potentially leading to further instability in the transportation industry. While indicators suggest transportation prices are stabilizing, the overall transportation environment remains unpredictable. Additionally, fuel prices have been unpredictable and may vary depending on economic activity in the areas where we ship and receive goods as well as prevailing oil prices. We have seen fuel prices increase due to recent military operations in and around Iran, which have led to volatility in the price of crude oil. Fuel prices could continue to remain volatile as the conflict persists.

paragraphs: 本公司面臨許多重大風險與不確定性，因此投資本公司普通股具有風險與不確定性。下列所述因素可能會對本公司業務、營運結果與財務狀況造成重大且不利的影響。雖然每項風險皆分別說明，但其中一些風險是相互關聯的，且某些風險可能觸發其他風險的適用性。此外，下列所述的風險與不確定性並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前本公司尚未知悉或認為不具重大性，也可能潛在地影響本公司業務、營運結果與財務狀況。投資人應考量下列因素，並配合本報告中包含的其他資訊，包括第二部分第七項「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析與討論—流動性與資本運用」，以決定是否購買本公司普通股。

本公司產品製造所使用的原料之可得性與成本，會受到作物產量與收成量波動的影響，而這些波動是由我們無法控制的因素所導致。這些原料包括花生、山核桃、杏仁、腰果、核桃、松子及其他堅果、壓碎燕麥、乾果與種子、可可、蛋白、以及用於製造本公司產品的其他植物油與產品。我們無法控制的因素包括惡劣天氣條件、自然災害（包括洪水、豪雨、冰雹、泥石流、龍捲風、乾旱、霜害、地震與颶風）、氣候模式變動、農業病蟲害、外幣波動、貿易協議、關稅與禁運、進出口管制、其他作物價格、勞工短缺、通貨膨脹條件、政治變動與動盪、制裁、罷工、來源規範變更、武裝衝突（如烏克蘭與中東地區的衝突）、燃料價格變動、全球客戶需求變動、疫情與疾病、政府農業計畫變動、政府對任何農產品的支持、聯邦與州政府針對前述事項或其它事項的命令，以及某些國家（包括中國與印度）的購買新行為。此外，美國農業部（USDA）或其他政府機構的任何決定，也可能減少本公司產品所使用的可食用堅果及其他原料的供應，並可能（除其他事項外）導致本公司成本顯著增加。這些決定包括但不限於：某些農民使用的農藥、除草劑或其他化學品在作物上留下有害殘留、對環境造成負面影響、導致或可能導致健康問題、任何作物部分受到黃曲毒素或其他物質污染，或任何未來原料或產品因其他原因而召回。

由於這些原料為大宗商品，其價格由市場決定，因此可能因多種事件（如上述所述）而迅速且劇烈波動。此外，本公司無法對堅果大宗商品價格變動進行避險，因為目前尚無適當的期貨、衍生品或其他風險共擔市場，本公司亦無法建立這樣的市場。因此，為達成或維持利潤水平，本公司試圖提高產品價格以反映所使用原料成本的增加。然而，本公司可能無法成功地將部分或全部的價格增加轉嫁給客戶，甚至完全無法轉嫁。此外，即使本公司成功地將部分或全部的價格增加轉嫁給客戶，也可能無法在合適的時間內完成。本公司提高價格的能力與任何價格增加的時間，往往取決於競爭對手的行動，而部分競爭對手規模較大且多元化程度較高，或擁有生產這些原料的農場。確定大宗商品成本與客戶價格的對應關係，也需要本公司整個運營過程中的大量協調，而本公司可能無法在未來成功管理這種協調，以對應大宗商品成本與客戶價格。本公司已觀察到包裝及其他用於製造與包裝本公司產品的產品的快速通貨膨脹，以及難以預測的一般通貨膨脹條件，且本公司可能無法將這些通貨膨脹增加轉嫁給客戶，或可能無法在合適的時間內完成。本公司也觀察到關稅及關稅威脅，導致價格增加或不確定的變化，以及本公司所處市場的不確定性，包括購買某些製造產品的設備。此外，本公司能夠轉嫁給客戶的任何產品價格增加，最終可能減少本公司產品的需求與銷售，因為客戶減少購買、購買較低價位的產品或較低毛利的產品。另一方面，如果任何原料的價格顯著下降，且本公司手中持有這些原料的庫存，本公司可能無法降低產品價格，而不會對毛利率造成不利影響，或客戶不會轉嫁價格下降，這可能會影響這些產品的總體需求。任何購買這些原料的競爭對手或擁有生產這些原料農場的競爭對手，可能能夠更迅速地降低價格，而本公司可能失去市場份額。本公司也面臨購買大部分堅果、花生與核桃直接來自農民的風險，包括購買這些產品時的價格可能因市場條件改變而高於當時的市場價格。因此，因為本公司在收穫季節直接從農民處購買大部分堅果、花生與核桃，並在會計年度內進行剝殼與加工，因此有機會在取得這些堅果後，市場條件可能惡化。根據這些變動的市場條件，本公司可能被迫以低於取得成本的價格出售這些堅果。任何上述因素之一或更多，都可能對本公司營運結果、現金流與財務狀況造成重大不利影響。

此外，堅果市場價格的波動可能影響本公司庫存價值、毛利與利潤。本公司與部分商業原料客戶簽訂固定價格承諾。這些承諾的有效期間通常為三個月至十二個月。有效期間為六個月或以上的承諾，在會計年度2026年約佔本公司年度淨銷售額的1%。有時本公司會在確定取得成本前，就某些堅果產品與客戶簽訂固定價格承諾，以維持客戶關係，或在管理層判斷市場或收穫條件如此需要時。若本公司如此做，且固定價格與取得成本未適當對應，這些固定價格承諾可能導致毛利減少或負毛利，這可能會對本公司財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響。

本公司處於高度競爭的環境中。競爭的主要領域包括風味、品質、包裝、價格、營養、品牌認知度、廣告、促銷、便利性與服務。本公司主要產品與許多區域性、國家性與國際性公司的食品與零食產品競爭，其中一些公司規模較大且資源更豐富，例如Hormel Foods Corp.（Planters品牌）、Diamond Brand、General Mills（Nature Valley品牌）、PepsiCo, Inc.（Quaker品牌）、Mondelez（CLIF品牌）、Kellanova（NutriSystem品牌）、以及其他公司。某些其他雜貨零售商，例如國際商店或小型格式商店，可能不會販售本公司產品。其他小型競爭對手可能能夠專注於成長較快的利基市場，而本公司因規模、運營、行銷策略或對本公司公司的看法，無法有效地行銷或銷售給這些市場。此外，某些食品零售商與網際網路零售商可能尋求投資服務某些利基市場的公司，並以提供貨架空間、增加促銷活動或其他行銷努力來換取這些公司的股權，而本公司無法提供給這些食品零售商或網際網路公司。近年來堅果與零食食品產業的合併與收購活動增加，使市場的競爭價格壓力更加強烈。許多競爭對手透過公開市場購買堅果，因此不受直接從農民處以固定價格購買殼堅果、花生、核桃及其他堅果類的風險影響。本公司也與商業原料市場中的其他剝殼商競爭，以及與零售與批發市場中的區域加工商競爭。為維持或增加市場份額，本公司必須持續以競爭性價格銷售產品，並投資於行銷、廣告、新產品創新與貨架空間與置位費用。這可能會導致毛利率下降，如果本公司無法增加銷售量或以其他方式降低成本，這可能會對本公司財務狀況與營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。

某些客戶的採購決定，包括某些最大的私有品牌客戶，是基於定期競標程序，其中成功的單一投標者可確保在食品零售商、超級市場、批發商、俱樂部商店或網際網路零售商處銷售所選產品或產品，直到下一次競標程序，排除其他投標者。如果本公司投標過高而失去透過這些渠道銷售產品的權利，即使只是暫時，本公司銷售量可能顯著下降。另一方面，如果本公司投標成功但價格低於本公司期望的價格點，本公司可能會降低毛利率。此外，如果大宗商品價格或其他投入價格隨後上升，而客戶不願或無法接受價格上漲，本公司毛利率可能進一步下降。堅果與零食食品產業近年來經歷了合併與大量收購活動。如果某些競爭對手選擇降低價格以增加銷售或市場份額，本公司市場份額可能下降，這可能會對本公司財務狀況與營運結果造成不利影響。
